rules.title: Newark rent control ordinance (Title XIX, ch. 19:2)
rules.requirement: At lease expiration a landlord may not raise rent by more than the CPI-U (NY-NJ area) change over the prior 15 months to 3 months, and never more than 4%. No annual increase is allowed if the unit is not in substantial compliance with codes or the landlord has not registered.
rules.key_value: CPI-U increase, capped at 4% per 12 months
rules.coverage_conditions: All multiple dwellings (any building with one or more rented apartments or units) in Newark
rules.exemptions: Public housing; hotel/motel transient space; commercial space; newly constructed multiple dwellings for up to 30 years from completion (or the initial mortgage amortization period if shorter) once certified (19:2-18.1); substantially rehabilitated vacant dwellings for 5 years (19:2-18.2); Rental Rehabilitation Program units with Section 8; units under a government rent-regulation contract
rules.quoted_span: In no case shall the allowable rent increase exceed 4%.
rules.interaction: Local rent control; the NJ Anti-Eviction Act and state law on rent control exemptions (N.J.S.A. 2A:42-84.1 et seq.) apply alongside it.

all.unavailable: Rent Control Board certification of newly constructed multiple dwelling exemption

any.unavailable: public housing, transient hotel/motel space, commercial use, rental-rehabilitation Section 8 units, government rent-regulation contract, or substantially rehabilitated vacant dwelling exempt for 5 years

notes: Rate section (19:2-3) amended 9-18-2024 by Ord. 6PSF-I; effective_date uses that adoption date (no separate effective date printed).
